## Purpose and Entry Points
Isoflow is a React/TypeScript diagram-editor library for creating network/architecture diagrams with icons, regions, connectors, and text. Its public editor root is `src/Isoflow.tsx`; package/browser bootstraps are `src/index.tsx` and `src/standaloneExports.ts`. Runnable integration examples—including editable, readonly, and debug variants—are under `src/examples/index.tsx`.

## Editor Composition and Rendering
`src/Isoflow.tsx` assembles the editor’s providers, canvas, overlays, and controls. `src/components/Renderer/Renderer.tsx` is the scene-facing rendering boundary, while `src/components/SceneLayer/SceneLayer.tsx` organizes SVG scene layers. Concrete model content is rendered by ordered layer components:
- `src/components/SceneLayers/Nodes/Nodes.tsx`
- `src/components/SceneLayers/Connectors/Connectors.tsx`
- `src/components/SceneLayers/Rectangles/Rectangles.tsx`
- `src/components/SceneLayers/TextBoxes/TextBoxes.tsx`

## Model, Views, and State Boundaries
Persistent diagram data is centered on a model store, scene store, and transient UI-state store: `src/stores/modelStore.tsx`, `src/stores/sceneStore.tsx`, and `src/stores/uiStateStore.tsx`. Reducers isolate mutations for model items, connectors, rectangles, text boxes, views, and layer ordering in `src/stores/reducers/index.ts` and related reducer modules. Hooks such as `src/hooks/useModelItem.ts`, `src/hooks/useConnector.ts`, and `src/hooks/useView.ts` provide component-level access rather than coupling UI directly to stores.

## Validation and Import/Initialization
Diagram input is typed and runtime-validated through schemas in `src/schemas/index.ts`, `src/schemas/model.ts`, and `src/schemas/validation.ts`. `src/hooks/useInitialDataManager.ts` is the initialization boundary for supplied diagram data. This separates the library’s external data contract from internal normalized state and enables consumers to supply initial models, icons, colors, and views.

## Interaction and Editing Pipeline
`src/interaction/useInteractionManager.ts` selects and coordinates pointer/keyboard behavior. Mode modules implement discrete canvas operations: dragging (`src/interaction/modes/DragItems.ts`), panning (`src/interaction/modes/Pan.ts`), lasso selection (`src/interaction/modes/Lasso.ts`), connector creation (`src/interaction/modes/Connector.ts`), icon placement (`src/interaction/modes/PlaceIcon.ts`), and rectangle/text operations. Transform UI is separated into `src/components/TransformControlsManager/TransformControlsManager.tsx` and item-specific transform controls, while `src/components/ItemControls/ItemControlsManager.tsx` exposes selected-item editing panels.

## Geometry, Projection, and Export
Coordinate and isometric projection logic are concentrated in `src/hooks/useIsoProjection.ts`, `src/utils/CoordsUtils.ts`, and `src/utils/SizeUtils.ts`; connector routing has a dedicated `src/utils/pathfinder.ts` boundary. Export UI is `src/components/ExportImageDialog/ExportImageDialog.tsx`, with export options/utilities in `src/utils/exportOptions.ts` and `src/utils/renderer.ts`. Rendering uses SVG-oriented components such as `src/components/Svg/Svg.tsx`.

## Runtime, Delivery, and External Surface
The core runtime is React with TypeScript, bundled by Webpack configurations in `webpack/dev.config.js` and `webpack/prod.config.js`. A standalone Docker-oriented entry/build path exists in `src/index-docker.tsx`, `webpack/docker.config.js`, and `Dockerfile`. Documentation is a separate Next.js application under `docs/pages/index.tsx`. External integration is primarily npm consumption (`isoflow` plus icon-pack packages), custom icon libraries, image/code export, and optional Docker distribution; no backend service is represented in the repository.
